In a vibrant atmosphere full of youth energy and enthusiasm, we celebrated the closing ceremony of the “A Step Makes a Difference” campaign, bringing together around 150 young people from refugee, migrant, and Egyptian communities. Led by youth under the East African Migration Routes (EAMR) Project, implemented by Save the Children, and supported by the Government of Switzerland, the campaign aimed to raise awareness of alternative education and career pathways for young people. The event showcased the campaign’s digital achievements, inspiring success stories, a panel discussion, and interactive activities led by youth. A partners’ exhibition also connected participants with job, training, and volunteering opportunities through organizations including Life Makers, Career 180, Gzour for Development, Volunteer Hub, and Remote Coders. The celebration concluded with certificate distribution and recognition of the youth campaigners for their impactful contributions. #OneStepMakesADifference #EAMR_Youth_Campaigners In an atmosphere full of youthful enthusiasm and energy, we celebrated the closing ceremony of the “A Step Apart” campaign, with the participation of about 150 young men and women, refugees, immigrants, and Egyptians. The youth-led campaign was implemented within the Migration Pathways in East Africa project, implemented by Save the Children with support from the Government of Switzerland, with the aim of enhancing youth awareness of alternative educational and professional opportunities and opening new horizons for their future. The event witnessed the presentation of the most prominent results of the digital campaign, inspiring success stories, a discussion session and interactive activities led by youth, in addition to an exhibition of partners who provided job, training and volunteer opportunities for young people, including Life Makers, Career 180, Roots for Development, Volunteer Hub and Remote Coders. The day concluded with honoring the young people who carried out the campaign and distributing certificates in appreciation of their efforts and positive impact on their communities. #A step that makes a difference

Strengthening national systems is the basis of a sustainable response to the needs of refugees and host communities. Within the framework of cooperation with the Egyptian government, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees provided two magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) machines to support public hospitals in Egypt and contribute to the development of health care services that benefit both refugees and Egyptians. This contribution comes at a crucial time, as Egypt responds to increasing humanitarian and health needs as a result of the Sudan and Gaza crises, which has led to an increase in the number of people in need of basic health services in various parts of the country. With Egypt hosting more than 1.1 million refugees and asylum seekers from more than 60 nationalities, UNHCR and its partners are working alongside the Egyptian authorities to ensure that the health system keeps pace with the growing needs of refugees and members of the host community alike. By investing in public hospitals, UNHCR is contributing to building a more inclusive and equitable health system, ensuring that access to life-saving health care leaves no one behind. Read more:

CARE Egypt concluded a specialized training program in 3D printing and design technology, within the project “Creating a supportive educational environment for refugee children in Egypt,” with the participation of a group of Palestinian and Egyptian children. This training course was the result of a partnership between CARE Egypt and the Pixmakers Academy, affiliated with the Pixology Foundation for Peace and Development in the United States of America, and with support from UNICEF Egypt and UNICEF Egypt within the framework of enhancing quality learning opportunities for children and providing educational paths related to future skills. During the training, the children learned about the basics of printing technology and 3D design, and how to transform ideas into printable digital models, in addition to developing creative thinking, problem-solving, and teamwork skills. The children’s interactions and completed work reflected a remarkable level of enthusiasm and commitment, with the support of the Learning Space team and facilitators. CARE Egypt confirms its continued provision of innovative educational programs that contribute to empowering children and creating a supportive and safe educational environment, thus enhancing their opportunities for learning, integration, and building a better future.

At a time when humanitarian needs are increasing around the world, the UNHCR Zakat Fund for Refugees continues to transform zakat and charity into direct support that protects refugee and displaced families and restores hope to them. 🤍 During 2025: Zakat and charity support has reached more than one million people in 25 countries. More than 579 thousand refugees and displaced persons eligible for Zakat were able to secure food, rent, medicine, and education for their children. About 453 thousand people benefited from charity to meet urgent needs and build their families’ resilience. For a family forced to flee, zakat may mean a safe roof, life-saving treatment, or an educational opportunity that restores hope for the future. Deserving refugees are included among the legitimate Zakat recipients, which makes your giving a direct means of protecting them and preserving their dignity. Since 2017, the Fund has contributed to supporting about 9.9 million people around the world, according to a policy of distributing 100% of Zakat funds and with a full commitment to transparency and Sharia compliance. Your giving makes a real difference. Learn about the impact stories and results of 2025 in the annual report on Islamic philanthropy, and be part of the hope.

Most people think of “Heart Health” as cardio and kale. But at First Aid Responders, we know that the heart is also fueled by how we connect with one another. Active Listening: Giving someone your undivided attention is the rarest gift. Non-Judgment: A healthy heart needs a safe space to breathe and be honest. Recognition: Validating someone’s effort 🧠is like a shot of oxygen for their soul. This Valentine’s Day, let us protect each other’s hearts, physically and emotionally. Which of these 3 “Acts of Love” do for you need more of today? Tell us in the comments! In “Valentine’s” this year, we always focus on heart health from a medical standpoint, such as blood pressure and exercise...but we see that heart health also begins with “psychological comfort” and the way we deal with those we love. Active listening: You listen by concentrating on what is in front of you and giving your full attention.. This is the greatest gift. Containment without judgement: The heart needs a safe space in which it feels that it is accepted as it is, without blame. 🫀 Appreciation and gratitude: You see the effort of those in front of you and appreciate them.. This gives positive energy to the heart and soul. When we take care of our mental health, we reduce stress and this immediately affects our physical heart health. What is the most important trait that you try to apply in your life? #firstaidcertified #mentalhealthmatters #firstaidresponder #egypt #ValentinesDay2026
